description.value: Housed in the beautifully preserved 1912 E&N Duncan Train Station, the Cowichan Valley Museum and Archives sits in the picturesque Charles Hoey V.C. Memorial Park, surrounded by totem poles and gardens in the heart of Duncan. Operated by the Cowichan Historical Society since 1974, the museum offers curated artifact displays tracing the valley's history from Indigenous heritage to Duncan's origins as a 19th-century railway crossing. Admission is by donation, making it a welcoming cultural stop on any Cowichan Valley cycling itinerary.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is live and content-rich, confirming the museum's identity, address (130 Canada Avenue, Duncan, BC), and phone number (250) 746-6612. The contact page mentions free car parking (lot to north, street parking on Duncan Street) but neither the contact page nor any other subpage mentions bike racks, washrooms, water access, or any cyclist-specific amenities, so those remain null per absence-of-evidence rules. Two different postal codes appear on the website (V9L 3Y2 on the front page, V9L 1T4 on the contact page), flagged as a concern.
concerns: Two different postal codes appear on the website: V9L 3Y2 (front page) and V9L 1T4 (contact page) — the correct postal code should be verified before publication.
Website still shows a GoDaddy placeholder account (filler@godaddy.com) in the navigation, suggesting the site is newly built and some content or configuration may be incomplete.
OSM record contains no phone number; phone was sourced from website only.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, active cultural attraction in a historic train station at the centre of Duncan — a natural stop for touring cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley. Admission by donation lowers the barrier to entry.

wow_evidence: Museum in the 1912 E&N Duncan station amid the totem-pole park; heritage-museum band.
blurb: Valley museum in Duncan's 1912 train station, ringed by the city's totem poles.
